record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Steady states for nonlocal conflict-generation model
record.original_question: For the same nonlocal conflict-generation model ∂_t k_i = u_i g,R Σ_j=1^n ρ_ij u_j − (μ + βu_i)k_i, in what sense do spatially non-constant steady states exist under periodic boundary conditions with a top-hat detection function, and what qualitative properties do those steady states possess?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 18. In what sense do spatially non-constant steady state solutions exist associated to problem (2.16) subject to periodic boundary conditions and a top-hat detection function in a bounded domain? What qualitative properties do these solutions hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a bounded spatial domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with periodic boundary conditions, and fix $n \geq 1$ populations with densities $u_1,\dots,u_n : \Omega \times [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ (assumed given, e.g., as positive constants or as solutions of an accompanying movement system). For each pair $(i,j)$ let $\rho_{ij} \geq 0$ be interaction coefficients, and let $\mu, \beta > 0$ be decay constants. Define the spatial nonlocal averaging operator $g_{,R}$ with top-hat detection kernel of radius $R > 0$ by
$$ (g_{,R} f)(x) = \frac{1}{|B_R(0)|}\int_{B_R(0)} f(x+y)\, dy, $$
extended periodically. Consider the system of cognitive/conflict-memory variables $k_i : \Omega \times [0,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}$, $i=1,\dots,n$, governed by
$$ \partial_t k_i(x,t) \;=\; u_i(x,t)\; g_{,R}\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^n \rho_{ij}\, u_j\right)\!(x,t)\;-\;\bigl(\mu + \beta\, u_i(x,t)\bigr)\, k_i(x,t), \qquad i=1,\dots,n, $$
on $\Omega$ with periodic boundary conditions.

Problem. Determine in what precise sense (e.g., existence, multiplicity, regularity, bifurcation from the spatially homogeneous branch) there exist spatially non-constant stationary solutions $\{k_i^*(x)\}_{i=1}^n$ of the above system on $\Omega$ with the top-hat kernel of radius $R$, and characterize their qualitative properties (such as symmetry, monotonicity, dependence on $R$, $\mu$, $\beta$, and on the interaction matrix $(\rho_{ij})$, the location and stability of the bifurcations producing them, and their asymptotic shape as $R \to 0$ or $R \to \infty$).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as an open problem in a 2022/2023 survey on PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement. Related work studies stability/bifurcation for nonlocal predator–prey and cognitive-map models with top-hat kernels (showing destabilization of homogeneous states for appropriate detection radii), but no work appears to give a complete characterization of spatially non-constant steady states with their qualitative properties for this specific conflict-generation system under periodic boundary conditions with a top-hat kernel. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on nonlocal cognitive-map PDE models, including steady states under periodic boundary conditions with top-hat detection.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed explicitly as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Stability and bifurcation analysis for a general nonlocal predator–prey system with top-hat kernel function
status_evidence.snippet: Larger nonlocal competition radius with top-hat kernel triggers spatiotemporal patterns via bifurcation; small radius preserves stability.
status_evidence.claim: Related top-hat nonlocal models show bifurcations to non-constant steady states, but not for the precise conflict-generation system.

status_evidence.title: Cognitive Consumer-Resource Spatiotemporal Dynamics with Nonlocal Perception
status_evidence.snippet: Top-hat detection destabilizes homogeneous steady state for appropriate detection scale, unlike Gaussian/Laplacian kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for related cognitive-map models with top-hat kernels.
